A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IPMF research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including content moved between sections.

before.justification: v3 reports original Gaussian simulations, Swiss-roll experiments, SB benchmark evaluations, and image translation results on colored MNIST and CelebA.

after.justification: v4 retains these original simulations and experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix E, alongside explicitly attributed results from other work.

M1.justification: The alternating reciprocal, Markovian, and IPF projections remain unchanged, as do the DSBM/ASBM implementations and coupling initialization procedures. Corrected projection annotations and expanded mathematical explanations do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gaussian, Swiss-roll, SB mixture benchmark, colored MNIST, and CelebA tasks and initialization scenarios. The new discussion of multi-marginal SB and scientific applications does not introduce evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 4 retain identical comparator membership, including the DSBM/ASBM initialization variants, the benchmark-best row, and SF2M-Sink. Although v4 newly names SF2M-Sink in the experimental prose, its results already appeared in both corresponding v3 tables.

E3.justification: The data splits, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, and inference settings are retained. Table 6 is unchanged, as are the Gaussian experiment's three intermediate time points and 100 IPMF steps. Generalizing the theoretical time grid does not change the experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The initialization comparisons, Swiss-roll trajectory analysis, marginal-fitting evaluation, and CelebA FID/CMMD/MSE iteration analyses are retained. v3 Figure 7 becomes v4 Figure 6 with the same curves; the new explanatory discussion adds no ablation or robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The benchmark's Monte Carlo estimation procedures and sample counts remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1, 2, 4, and 5 are identical, and all embedded figure images are unchanged. Section 4.4 newly asserts faster convergence with SDEdit, referring to retained iteration curves. This is a limited addition to the stated qualitative findings, without new measurements.

T1.justification: v4 adds Theorem 3.3 and Appendix D.7's argument for weak convergence with bounded-support marginals. It also extends the multidimensional discrete Gaussian analysis from one intermediate time point to a general finite grid and revises contraction bounds, including the continuous one-dimensional factor in Lemma D.9. These substantially change the formal scope and derivations.

C1.justification: v3's theoretical contribution claims Gaussian convergence while conjecturing broader convergence. v4's introduction additionally presents discrete-time convergence for bounded-support marginals as an established contribution. This materially broadens the claimed guarantee, while retaining the unification and initialization-tradeoff claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds a copula-based explanation of the projections, an Identity-coupling optimality hypothesis, and qualifications that SDEdit only partially supports the intended improvements, with possible training-time savings. Appendices A–B add prospective multi-marginal applications and domain-specific motivation. The central quality/similarity interpretation and unrestricted-convergence limitation remain.

D1.justification: v3 Appendix C and v4 Appendix E provide the same architectures, optimization details, preprocessing, SDEdit settings, resource links, licenses, hardware, and training-time estimates. The implementation disclosures are relocated and lightly edited without substantive additions or revisions.

R1.justification: Section 3.2 adds an explicit comparison with prior IPF/IMF convergence guarantees and explains the claimed novelty of arbitrary initialization. Additional citations support focused discussions of multi-marginal SB and domain-specific applications. These expand the existing positioning without replacing its central IPF/IMF framing.

P1.justification: The theoretical appendix undergoes extensive explanatory rewriting, notation revision, and regrouping of multidimensional analysis and proofs before the one-dimensional material. Discussion moves into Appendix A, an appendix contents guide and motivation section are added, and v4 revises front matter, citation style, and numerous passages throughout.

P2.justification: The same seven figures and six tables are retained with resizing, reflow, and relocation. The Inverted 7 illustration moves from the main text to Appendix E.8; metric-direction arrows are added to CelebA tables, and the iteration-plot captions correctly identify ASBM panels previously labeled DSBM. The underlying graphics are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 expands the Gaussian analysis and clarifies research positioning, but its important new bounded-support theorem is not fully justified as written. Appendix D.7 establishes one subsequence converging to the SB in Equation 78, then concludes full convergence without ruling out other limit points. This gap in a newly advertised core contribution prevents a reliable net-quality judgment despite the explanatory gains; the empirical evidence remains unchanged.
